{{short description|Danish mathematician}}
'''Troels Jørgensen''' is a Danish mathematician at [[Columbia University]] working on [[hyperbolic geometry]] and [[complex analysis]], who proved [[Jørgensen's inequality]]. He wrote his thesis in 1970 at the [[University of Copenhagen]] under the joint supervision of [[Werner Fenchel]] and [[Bent Fuglede]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=29632}}</ref>

==Work==
He is known for [[Jørgensen's inequality]],<ref>{{Citation | last1=Jørgensen | first1=Troels | title=On discrete groups of Möbius transformations | jstor=2373814 | mr=0427627 | year=1976 | journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] | issn=0002-9327 | volume=98 | issue=3 | pages=739–749 | doi=10.2307/2373814}}</ref> and for his discovery of a [[hyperbolic 3-manifold|hyperbolic structure]] on certain [[Surface bundle over the circle|fibered 3-manifolds]]<ref>{{cite journal | last=Jørgensen |first=Troels |title=Compact 3-manifolds of constant negative curvature fibering over the circle |zbl=0368.53025 |journal=Ann. Math. (2) | volume=106 |pages=61–72 | year=1977}}</ref> which were one of the inspirations for [[William Thurston]]'s [[Geometrisation Conjecture]].<ref>{{Citation | last1=Thurston | first1=William P. | author1-link=William Thurston | title=Three-dimensional manifolds, Kleinian groups and hyperbolic geometry | doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1982-15003-0 | year=1982 | journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |series=New Series | issn=0002-9904 | volume=6 | issue=3 | pages=357–381 | mr=648524| doi-access=free }}, p. 362</ref> He is also credited with being one of the co-discoverers of the ordered structure of the set of volumes of hyperbolic 3-manifolds.<ref>Thurston, loc. cit., Theorem 3.5 on p. 364</ref><ref>{{Citation
| last  = Gromov
| first = Michael
| author-link = Mikhael Gromov (mathematician)
| chapter = Hyperbolic manifolds according to Thurston and Jorgensen
| date = 1981
| title  = Semin. Bourbaki, 32e annee, Vol. 1979/80
| publisher = Signature Books
| publication-date = 1981
| series=Lect. Notes Math.
| number= 842
|pages=40–53
|zbl=0452.51017
}}</ref>
